ai_advisor.executive_summary: Three security issues found for Deployment sandbox-kata/target-kata: service account token automount enabled, writable root filesystem, and setuid/setgid binaries in the image. These increase attack surface and persistence risk; fixes require operator validation before applying.
ai_advisor.remediation_overview: Prioritize disabling service account token automount and making root filesystem read-only after verifying workload needs and writable paths. Remove setuid/setgid binaries via image rebuild. All fixes are manual-review or operator-approved due to compatibility risk.

prioritized_groups.title: Credentials exposure (highest)
prioritized_groups.rationale: Service account tokens in-pod enable lateral movement and API access; high severity and blast radius.

prioritized_groups.title: Immutable filesystem (high)
prioritized_groups.rationale: Writable root increases attack persistence and tampering; enabling readOnlyRootFilesystem mitigates but may break app.

prioritized_groups.title: Image hardening (medium)
prioritized_groups.rationale: Setuid/setgid binaries enable privilege escalation; requires image rebuild and validation.

item_advice.explanation: Pod mounts a service account token, allowing in-pod access to Kubernetes API and cluster credentials exposure.
item_advice.operator_impact: Disabling automount breaks any code in the pod that calls Kubernetes API (controllers, sidecars, or tooling).
item_advice.validation_advice: Audit pod containers for Kubernetes client usage, mounted config or secrets; test after disabling in a staging replica before production.
item_advice.ordering_reason: Credentials exposure poses the largest immediate risk; verify API usage before changing.

item_advice.explanation: Container root filesystem is writable, permitting persistence and tampering of binaries/config in runtime.
item_advice.operator_impact: Enabling readOnlyRootFilesystem may break writes to /tmp, /var, application data paths; must provision explicit writable volumes first.
item_advice.validation_advice: Identify writable paths (including /tmp, /var/tmp, workspace mounts); convert them to dedicated volumes (emptyDir) and validate app behavior in staging.
item_advice.ordering_reason: Hardening filesystem reduces persistence risk but depends on moving writable paths first to avoid downtime.

item_advice.explanation: Image contains setuid/setgid binaries which can be abused for privilege escalation inside the container.
item_advice.operator_impact: Removing these binaries requires rebuilding images and may remove admin utilities relied on by operators or apps.
item_advice.validation_advice: Rebuild image from a minimal base, remove unnecessary setuid/setgid files, then run integration tests and deploy to staging before rollout.
item_advice.ordering_reason: Image changes are more involved; perform after addressing immediate exposure and filesystem hardening.

ai_advisor.guided_operator_message: Review and validate each remediation in staging: disable automount only if pod doesn't need API access, convert writable paths to volumes before readOnlyRootFilesystem, and rebuild images to remove setuid/setgid binaries.
warnings: Do not disable automount without confirming Kubernetes API usage by the workload.
Making root filesystem read-only will break apps that write to OS paths unless writable volumes are provided.
Removing setuid/setgid binaries requires image rebuild and may alter expected tooling behavior.
next_steps: Inventory in-pod Kubernetes API usage and determine if service account token is required.
Map application writable paths and create explicit volumes for them (emptyDir or PVC) in a staging deployment.
Test disabling automount in staging once API usage is ruled out.
Test enabling readOnlyRootFilesystem in staging after provisioning writable volumes.
